lead: Huntington Beach plumbing deals with hard water, salt air and 1960s and 1970s slab homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Huntington Beach.
risk: slab leaks and pinhole leaks in aging copper, salt-air corrosion and hard water scale
risk_short: slab leaks, corrosion and hard water
why: Huntington Beach boomed in the 1960s and 1970s, so many homes have copper lines under the slab that now leak. Pinhole leaks in that copper are a common call.
Salt air near the coast corrodes outdoor fittings, hose bibs and water heater parts. California requires water heaters to be strapped for earthquakes.
water: Huntington Beach pumps most of its water from the Orange County groundwater basin and buys the rest through the Metropolitan Water District. It is hard.
tips: Strap your water heater for earthquakes.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
After repeat pinhole leaks, ask about a repipe.
Rinse and check outdoor fittings for corrosion.
areas: PipeMend works Downtown and in Huntington Harbour, the Bluffs, Seacliff, Edwards Hill, Sunset Beach and every other Huntington Beach neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the Huntington Beach Community Development Department, and plumbing contractors need a CSLB license with a C-36 classification.

faq.q: Why do Huntington Beach homes get slab leaks?
faq.a: Many homes were built in the 1960s and 1970s with copper lines under the slab. After 50-plus years, the copper wears thin. A hot spot on the floor or a moving meter are common signs.
